name: Collard Greens
guide: Thin to one strong seedling; harvest outer leaves once 8-10 in and let the center keep producing. Steady moderate light and cool temps keep leaves tender.

name: Curly Kale
guide: Pick lower outer leaves first, leaving the crown to regrow for repeat harvests. Watch for aphids; rinse leaves and remove any yellowing growth.

name: Green Bok Choy
guide: Fast and forgiving; harvest the whole compact head at the base or take outer stalks as needed. Keep it cool and well-lit to prevent early bolting.

name: Green Cabbage
guide: Thin to a single plant per pod since it needs room to head up. Harvest when the head feels firm; check roots monthly and trim any browning.

name: Hon Tsai Tai
guide: Asian flowering brassica; snap off tender flower stems and leaves regularly to encourage more shoots. Quick and low-maintenance.

name: Lacinato Kale
guide: Dinosaur/Tuscan kale; harvest the lowest leaves first and leave the central rosette to keep producing for months. Tolerant of cool indoor temps.

name: Mini Broccoli
guide: Needs top (high-light) placement; cut the central head before buds open, then harvest side shoots that follow. Keep temps cool to avoid bolting.

name: Mini Cauliflower
guide: The fussiest brassica indoors; place in high light and harvest the head while curds are still tight and white. Sensitive to heat and irregular conditions.

name: Purple Bok Choy
guide: Same easy care as green bok choy with purple-tinged leaves; harvest whole or by outer stalk. Cool conditions prevent premature bolting.

name: Purple Kohlrabi
guide: Grown for tender leaves and small stems indoors rather than a large bulb; thin to one plant and harvest young. Trim roots monthly to fit the pod.

name: Tokyo Bekana
guide: Frilly mild Chinese cabbage; cut outer leaves continuously or harvest the loose head whole. Fast-growing and beginner-friendly.

name: White Kohlrabi
guide: Harvest the crisp young leaves and slim stems; full bulbs rarely form in a pod. Thin to a single seedling and keep light steady.

name: Bi-Color Sunflower
guide: Needs top high-light spot and support as it gets tall; harvest petals/shoots young or let one bloom for seeds. Pinch early to keep it compact.

name: Blue Cornflower
guide: Edible bachelor's button blooms; deadhead spent flowers to keep new buds coming. Easy and tolerant of average indoor light.

name: Borage
guide: Star-shaped edible blue flowers with cucumber flavor; pinch tips to bush out and pick blooms fresh. Vigorous, so harvest often.

name: Calendula
guide: Edible pot-marigold petals; deadhead regularly to prolong blooming. Very forgiving and good for beginners.

name: Canna Flower
guide: Large ornamental that is slow and demanding indoors; give it room and consistent light. Mostly grown for foliage and showy blooms, not eating.

name: Celosia Mix
guide: Plumed/cockscomb blooms that love high light; pinch early for more flower stems. Long-lasting and low-fuss once established.

name: Chamomile
guide: Pick the small daisy-like flower heads for tea once petals are fully open. Frequent harvest encourages continued blooming.

name: Dianthus
guide: Clove-scented edible petals; deadhead to keep flowers coming. Compact and easy in medium light.

name: Marietta Marigold
guide: Edible, pest-deterring blooms; deadhead spent flowers and pinch tips to bush out. Reliable and beginner-friendly.

name: Nasturtium
guide: Both leaves and peppery flowers are edible; pinch to control trailing vines and harvest blooms often. Easy and productive.

name: Petunia
guide: Ornamental (non-edible) trailing blooms; deadhead regularly and pinch back leggy stems. Needs steady light for continuous flowering.

name: Portulaca Mix
guide: Heat- and light-loving succulent flower; thrives in the top zone and tolerates dry spells. Minimal care, just deadhead occasionally.

name: Purple Campanula
guide: Bellflower grown for ornamental blooms; deadhead to extend flowering. Slower to establish than annual flowers.

name: Purple Snapdragon
guide: Tall spikes that want high light; pinch the growing tip early for more flower stems and deadhead spent spikes. Edible blooms.

name: Red Hibiscus
guide: Grown for showy (and edible, for tea) blooms; slow to flower and needs consistent warmth and light. Prune to keep it manageable.

name: Red Impatiens
guide: Shade-tolerant ornamental blooms; deadhead and pinch to keep compact and full. Easy in medium light.

name: Stock Flower
guide: Fragrant edible spikes; place in high light and deadhead to prolong bloom. Pinch early for bushier growth.

name: Sunflower
guide: Top high-light placement and may need support; harvest shoots/petals young or let one head set edible seeds. Pinch to limit height.

name: Torenia
guide: Wishbone flower with continuous small blooms; pinch tips for fullness and deadhead lightly. Easy and shade-tolerant.

name: Viola
guide: Edible pansy-type flowers; pick blooms frequently to keep new buds forming. Compact, cool-loving, and beginner-friendly.

name: Zinnia
guide: Bright edible blooms that love high light; deadhead and cut flowers to encourage more. Pinch early for branching.

name: Banana Pepper
guide: High light required; hand-pollinate flowers by shaking or brushing, and remove the first few buds to build the plant. Prune and check roots monthly.

name: Cape Gooseberry
guide: Hand-pollinate and prune; eat fruit only once the husk papers off and it turns yellow-orange (green fruit is toxic). Needs high light and patience.

name: Cucumber
guide: Vigorous vine needing high light, support/trellising, and hand-pollination; harvest young and often to keep it producing. Prune side shoots to manage size.

name: Dragon Tongue Beans
guide: Self-pollinating bush bean; give it high light and support, and pick pods young for tenderness and continued set. Harvest frequently.

name: Green Beans
guide: Mostly self-pollinating; provide high light and a little support, and pick pods young to keep production going. Easier than the nightshade fruits.

name: Hungarian Hot Wax Pepper
guide: High light; hand-pollinate and remove early buds to strengthen the plant before fruiting. Harvest yellow for mild, leave longer for hotter/red.

name: Jalapeño
guide: Top high-light spot; hand-pollinate flowers and prune the first buds and lower leaves. Pick firm and dark green, or leave to redden for sweeter heat.

name: Lemon Hot Pepper
guide: One of the slowest peppers; high light, hand-pollination, and patience are essential. Remove first flowers early and prune to keep it productive.

name: Mini Eggplant
guide: High light and warmth; hand-pollinate flowers and prune to a few main stems. Harvest fruit while skin is still glossy.

name: Mini Okra
guide: Loves high light and warmth; harvest pods young (2-3 in) because they toughen fast. Pick frequently to keep pods coming.

name: Mini Pumpkin
guide: Sprawling vine that needs high light, support, and hand-pollination of separate male/female flowers. Limit to a couple of fruits per plant.

name: Mini Squash
guide: High light and hand-pollination required; harvest fruit young and often to keep the plant setting more. Prune leaves to manage the vine.

name: Peas
guide: Self-pollinating and cool-loving; give light support and pick pods young and often. Easier than the warm-season fruiting crops.

name: Poblano Pepper
guide: High light, hand-pollination, and pruning of early buds; harvest dark green and firm, or let ripen red. Slow but rewarding.

name: Purple Cayenne Pepper
guide: Ornamental-edible hot pepper; high light and hand-pollination needed. Harvest at desired color, removing first buds early to build the plant.

name: Red Cherry Tomato
guide: Hand-pollinate by shaking flowers; remove the first flower buds to encourage roots, prune yellow leaves, and check roots monthly. Harvest when evenly red and slightly soft to avoid cracking.

name: Red Mini Strawberry
guide: Slow to fruit; high light and hand-pollination of each flower are essential. Pinch early runners and harvest berries fully red.

name: Shishito Pepper
guide: Among the quicker peppers; high light and hand-pollination still needed. Harvest small and green for blistering, picking often to keep it producing.

name: Sweet Pepper
guide: High light, hand-pollination, and pruning of first buds; harvest green or leave to ripen to color for sweetness. Monitor for pests.

name: Thai Eggplant
guide: Warm- and high-light-loving; hand-pollinate and prune to a couple of stems. Harvest small round fruits while glossy and firm.

name: Yellow Cherry Tomato
guide: Same care as red cherry: hand-pollinate, remove first buds, prune yellowing leaves, and check roots monthly. Harvest when fully golden and slightly soft.

name: Yellow Mini Strawberry
guide: Slow, high-light fruiting plant needing per-flower hand-pollination. Remove early runners and harvest berries when fully colored and fragrant.

name: Catnip
guide: Vigorous mint-family herb; pinch tips often to keep it bushy and harvest leaves anytime. Very low-maintenance in low light.

name: Chervil
guide: Delicate anise-flavored herb that prefers cool, low light; snip outer leaves and harvest before it bolts. Best used fresh.

name: Chives
guide: Cut leaves to about an inch above the base and they regrow repeatedly. Nearly foolproof; harvest often to keep tender.

name: Cilantro
guide: Fast and easy; snip outer leaves and harvest frequently since it bolts in warmth. Keep cool to delay flowering.

name: Dill
guide: Harvest feathery fronds as needed; pinch the central stem to delay bolting. Tall, so trim to keep it tidy.

name: Garlic Chives
guide: Flat, garlicky leaves; cut near the base and they regrow for many harvests. Extremely easy and long-lived.

name: Genovese Basil
guide: Pinch above a leaf pair to force branching and remove flower buds to keep leaves coming. Harvest from the top regularly; never strip more than a third at once.

name: Holy Basil
guide: Tulsi prefers brighter, high-light placement; pinch tips and remove flowers to prolong leaf production. Aromatic and easy.

name: Italian Parsley
guide: Slow to germinate but long-producing; harvest outer stems at the base and let the center regrow. Pick often to keep it productive.

name: Lavender
guide: Slow to germinate and the trickiest herb indoors; needs high light and restrained watering. Harvest sprigs once established.

name: Lemon Balm
guide: Vigorous lemony mint-relative; pinch tips to keep bushy and harvest leaves freely. Remove flowers to maintain flavor.

name: Lemongrass
guide: Grows as a grassy clump; harvest outer stalks at the base once thickened. Slow to bulk up but undemanding.

name: Lime Basil
guide: Citrus-scented basil; pinch tips and remove flower buds to keep leaves tender. Harvest from the top frequently.

name: Mint
guide: Aggressive and forgiving; harvest sprigs from the top and pinch often to keep it compact. Thrives in low light.

name: Oregano
guide: Harvest sprigs once stems are 4-6 in; flavor strengthens as it matures. Pinch tips to encourage bushy growth.

name: Purple Basil
guide: Deep-purple basil; pinch above leaf pairs and remove flowers to extend harvest. Slightly slower than green basils.

name: Rosemary
guide: Slow to germinate and establish; harvest sprigs sparingly until the plant is robust. Don't overwater the woody stems.

name: Sage
guide: Woody herb that establishes slowly; harvest individual leaves and avoid over-picking young plants. Likes airflow and steady light.

name: Savory
guide: Peppery thyme-like herb; snip sprigs as needed and pinch to keep bushy. Easy and steady.

name: Shiso
guide: Japanese perilla; harvest individual leaves and pinch flower stalks to keep foliage coming. Vigorous and easy.

name: Stevia
guide: Sweet-leaf herb that wants high light; pinch tips to bush out and harvest leaves before flowering for best sweetness. Slower to establish.

name: Sweet Marjoram
guide: Mild oregano relative; snip sprigs once 4-6 in and pinch to encourage branching. Easy and aromatic.

name: Sweet Thai Basil
guide: Anise-scented basil; pinch above leaf pairs and remove flower buds to keep producing. Harvest from the top often.

name: Tarragon
guide: Harvest sprigs once established and pinch tips for bushiness; flavor improves as it matures. Slower than soft herbs.

name: Thyme
guide: Slow-growing woody herb; harvest sprigs sparingly while young and more freely once bushy. Don't overwater.

name: American Mustard
guide: Spicy green; harvest outer leaves young for milder flavor and pick often. Bolts in heat, so keep it cool.

name: Arugula
guide: Fast cut-and-come-again green; snip outer leaves at a few inches and it regrows. Harvest young for milder, less peppery flavor.

name: Bull's Blood Beet Greens
guide: Grown for deep-red tender leaves rather than roots; harvest baby leaves outer-first and pick often. Easy and colorful.

name: Bunching Onions
guide: Snip green tops as needed and they regrow repeatedly; no bulb forms. Very low-maintenance scallions.

name: Buttercrunch Lettuce
guide: Bibb-type; snip outer leaves once 4 in for continuous harvest or cut the whole head at maturity, leaving a third to regrow. Likes cool temps.

name: Butterhead Lettuce
guide: Tender loose head; harvest outer leaves continuously or cut the whole head at the base. Keep cool (60-70F) for sweet leaves.

name: Celery
guide: Slow and thirsty; harvest outer stalks as needed rather than the whole plant. Check roots monthly and keep light steady.

name: Endive
guide: Slightly bitter chicory; harvest outer leaves or the whole head. Cooler temps and steady light reduce bitterness.

name: Green Salanova Lettuce
guide: One-cut multi-leaf lettuce; harvest the whole rosette at the base or take outer leaves over time. Reliable and uniform.

name: Green Tatsoi
guide: Spoon-shaped Asian green; cut outer leaves continuously or harvest the whole rosette. Fast and beginner-friendly.

name: Iceberg Lettuce
guide: Tight crisphead that needs the longest of the lettuces and cool temps; harvest when the head feels firm. Trim browning roots monthly.

name: Lollo Rossa Lettuce
guide: Frilly red loose-leaf; snip outer leaves for continuous picking. Colors deepen with good light.

name: Muir Lettuce
guide: Heat-tolerant Batavia; snip outer leaves at 4 in or cut the dense head at maturity, leaving a third intact. Check and trim roots monthly.

name: Perpetual Spinach
guide: A chard grown like spinach; harvest outer leaves and it keeps producing for months without bolting. Very productive.

name: Purslane
guide: Succulent, lemony green; pinch stem tips and it regrows quickly. Tolerant and low-maintenance.

name: Radicchio
guide: Bitter chicory that heads slowly; cool temps improve color and reduce bitterness. Harvest the firm head at the base.

name: Red Amaranth
guide: Vivid red leaves harvested young as a cooking/salad green; pick outer leaves and tips often. Fast and easy.

name: Red Oak Leaf Lettuce
guide: Loose-leaf with lobed red leaves; cut-and-come-again from the outside. Mild and quick.

name: Red Romaine
guide: Upright red-tinged romaine; harvest outer leaves continuously or cut the whole head, leaving the base to regrow. Keep cool for crisp leaves.

name: Red Sails Lettuce
guide: Bronze-red loose-leaf that's slow to bolt; snip outer leaves as needed. One of the easiest lettuces.

name: Red Salad Bowl Lettuce
guide: Deeply lobed red oak-leaf type; cut-and-come-again from the outer leaves. Mild, tender, and fast.

name: Red Sorrel
guide: Tangy lemony leaves with red veining; harvest young outer leaves often. Vigorous and easy.

name: Red Swiss Chard
guide: Colorful, productive green; harvest outer stalks at the base and the center keeps producing for months. Very forgiving.

name: Red Tatsoi
guide: Purple-tinged Asian rosette green; harvest outer leaves continuously or cut whole. Fast and easy.

name: Romaine
guide: Gardyn's most popular plant; harvest outer leaves over weeks or cut the whole head, leaving a third to regrow. Keep cool for crisp, sweet leaves.

name: Watercress
guide: Peppery green that loves moisture; pinch stem tips and it regrows fast. Harvest often before flowering.

name: Wheatgrass
guide: Fastest crop in the catalog; harvest by cutting blades near the base when 6-8 in for juicing. One main cut, sometimes a smaller regrowth.

name: Yellow Swiss Chard
guide: Golden-stemmed chard; harvest outer stalks and the crown keeps producing. Hardy and long-lived.
